name: House price to residence-based earnings ratio (median and lower quartile)
variables: median and lower-quartile residence-based full-time earnings
latest_period: 2025 (house prices year ending Sep 2025; ASHE April 2025)
api_notes: Single workbook aff2ratioofhousepricetoresidencebasedearnings.xlsx at a stable /current/ URL; tables 5c (LA median) and 6c (LA lower quartile), 1c/2c (region, England). Parsed with zipfile + xml.etree.
limitations: Full-time residence-based earnings, not young entrants' pay; LA earnings are ASHE survey estimates with sampling noise. 2025 median ratios: Bedford 8.37, Central Bedfordshire 8.36, Luton 9.07 vs East of England 8.52 and England 7.64; lower quartile Bedford 9.10, Central Beds 9.35, Luton 9.81 vs England 6.99.
why_it_matters: Entry-level (lower-quartile) home ownership is less affordable in all three UAs than in England, which shapes whether NLW-paid resort staff can live near the site.

name: Price Index of Private Rents (PIPR): monthly average private rents by LA
api_notes: Latest workbook link scraped from the dataset page (dated folder, e.g. /21october2026/); Table 1 long format, time period as Excel date serial.
limitations: Stock of existing tenancies, so new-let rents a newcomer pays are typically higher; latest months provisional. Sep 2026 average rent: Bedford GBP 1,177 (1-bed 802), Central Bedfordshire 1,258 (870), Luton 1,231 (913); England 1,466 (1,199), East of England 1,298 (900).
why_it_matters: A one-bed private rent in the three UAs takes 39-44% of gross full-time NLW pay (GBP 24,784.50 a year), so housing cost is a real barrier to in-migrating workers.

name: Childcare providers and inspections: management information
variables: latest inspection outcomes (renewed EIF report-card areas and legacy grades)
next_release: Next quarterly extract (30 Sep 2026 data expected late 2026)
api_notes: Latest 'childcare provider data as at <date>' CSV found via the GOV.UK content API (https://www.gov.uk/api/content/government/statistical-data-sets/childcare-providers-and-inspections-management-information).
limitations: Management information, not official statistics. Excludes maintained nursery schools/classes, so understates early education capacity; places are registered capacity, not vacancies or hours. 30 Jun 2026: EYR places per 100 children aged 0-4 Bedford 42.9, Central Bedfordshire 39.5, Luton 25.4 vs East of England 46.0, England 43.8.
why_it_matters: Childcare capacity constrains how many economically inactive parents (25+) could take shift work at the resort; Luton has markedly fewer registered places per child.

name: Further education and skills inspections and outcomes: management information
variables: latest overall effectiveness before renewed EIF (1-4)
renewed EIF report-card grades by evaluation area
api_notes: 'as at <date>' provider-state CSV plus the renewed-EIF inspections CSV (10 Nov 2025 onwards), joined on Provider URN; attachments discovered via the GOV.UK content API.
limitations: Provider LA is head office, so national apprenticeship providers delivering locally are missed. No single overall grade under report cards (from 10 Nov 2025); legacy grades may be several years old. 16 providers recorded in the three UAs; all 14 with a legacy grade are Good; one (Intelligencia Training) has a report card, all areas at Expected standard.
why_it_matters: Shows the quality and thinness of the local FE/apprenticeship provider base that would deliver pre-employment and hospitality training for the resort.

name: GMCA Unit Cost Database v3.0 (fiscal value of moving claimants into work; NEET costs)
variables: fiscal benefit of UC jobseeker into work
NEET cost per year (fiscal and economic)
api_notes: Workbook https://www.greatermanchester-ca.gov.uk/media/sbdg15pr/gmca-unit-cost-database-v3-0-final.xlsx, sheet 'Employment & Economy'; values extracted to research/unit_costs.json.
limitations: Fiscal values are transfers (excluded from public value); NEET rows are 2010/11-based and rated lowest confidence; ESA value is 2017/18 modelling uprated; no UC health-claimant value. UC jobseeker into work GBP 17,736/yr, ESA claimant GBP 15,470/yr, NEET 18-24 GBP 6,325/yr fiscal (2025/26 prices).
quality: Curated secondary unit costs (HM Treasury Green Book supplementary guidance)
why_it_matters: Gives a defensible GBP value per local resident moved from benefits into resort jobs for the business case.

name: Local-hire outcomes at comparable large developments (compiled)
publisher: Various (DCMS Olympic meta-evaluation, LLDC, Battersea Power Station, Center Parcs, Disneyland Paris impact study, Eden Project)
api_notes: Compiled by hand into research/local_hire_benchmarks.json, each entry with its own source URL.
limitations: 'Local' is defined differently in every case (host boroughs, single borough, county, 15-mile radius), so shares are not directly comparable; several are operator claims, not independent monitoring. Center Parcs Woburn Forest (2014, 1,500 jobs): 90% live within 15 miles; London 2012 ODA construction: 17.5% host-borough residents vs 15% target; Westfield Stratford: ~3,000 unemployed Newham residents vs 2,000 target.
quality: Mixed: evaluation reports and monitoring data alongside operator press statements
why_it_matters: Benchmarks what a realistic local-recruitment target for the resort's ~8,050 operational jobs could be, and how much it depends on how 'local' is defined.
